name: Anti-Submarine Warfare Shallow Water Craft (ASW-SWC) Programme
variant: Arnala-class ASW corvette series (8-ship shallow-water craft tranche)

header.one_liner: GRSE-designed 8-ship shallow-water ASW corvette programme (Arnala class), split across GRSE and Goa Shipyard, filling India's littoral anti-submarine coverage gap; lead ship commissioned 2024, hulls completing through 2025-26.
header.maker: Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers (GRSE) — design + lead hulls; Goa Shipyard Limited (GSL) — follow-on hulls
header.indigenous_label: ~80% indigenous by value; sonar/AA weapons partly imported

what_it_is.prose: The Anti-Submarine Warfare Shallow Water Craft (ASW-SWC) programme is an Indian Navy acquisition to field a series of small, shallow-draft anti-submarine corvettes — the Arnala class — designed by Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers (GRSE) specifically to hunt submarines and undersea threats in India's coastal, shallow waters where large frigates and destroyers cannot operate effectively. The programme addresses a well-documented capability gap: growing adversary submarine fleets (notably Pakistan's expanding submarine force, and China's sea-based presence in the Indian Ocean) versus India's limited littoral ASW assets. The core 8-ship shallow-water craft order was split across GRSE (Kolkata) and Goa Shipyard Limited (GSL), which had earlier built related patrol-craft series. The ships carry a hull-mounted sonar and an integrated ASW suite — lightweight torpedo tubes, ASW rocket launchers, and variable-depth sonar on later hulls — plus a compact gun for self-defence. The programme is a flagship of indigenous littoral warship construction and complements the larger Nilgiri-class frigates and the P-75 submarine programme. Ship names follow coastal islands and historic naval anchor points (Arnala, Anjadip, etc.). The lead ship commissioned in 2024, with the remaining hulls commissioning on a rolling basis through 2025-26.

deployments_procurement.summary: The ASW-SWC programme runs in two linked tranches: an initial GRSE ASW-covette design and its follow-on expansion into an 8-ship shallow-water craft order (2019), split across GRSE and GSL. The lead ship commissioned in 2024 and subsequent hulls — the Arnala-class series — are commissioning through 2025-26. The class distributes across the Indian Navy's Eastern and Western Commands for coastal ASW patrol. Precise per-ship contract value is not uniformly published (broadly reported at ~₹1,500-1,600 crore per ship; values vary by yard/tranche — flagged as uncertain).

faq.question: What is the ASW-SWC programme?
faq.answer: The Anti-Submarine Warfare Shallow Water Craft (ASW-SWC) programme is an Indian Navy acquisition for a series of small, shallow-draft anti-submarine corvettes (the Arnala class), designed by GRSE to counter submarines in India's coastal shallow waters.

faq.question: Which shipyards build the ASW-SWC?
faq.answer: The 8-ship programme is split across Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers (GRSE), which designed the class and built the lead hulls, and Goa Shipyard Limited (GSL), which builds a tranche of the follow-on hulls.

faq.question: Why does India need shallow-water ASW ships?
faq.answer: Large frigates and destroyers are too large and deep-draft to effectively hunt submarines in India's shallow coastal waters and straits. These specialist ASW corvettes with hull-mounted sonar fill the littoral anti-submarine coverage gap, protecting ports, sea lanes and coastlines from submarine incursions.

faq.question: How many ASW-SWC ships are being built?
faq.answer: The core programme is an 8-ship shallow-water craft order (2019), split across GRSE and GSL, building on an earlier GRSE ASW-corvette design. The lead ship commissioned in 2024 and the remaining hulls are commissioning through 2025-26.
